title: Finite absolutely-continuous realization of Chewi f-divergence
source_anchor: Sinho Chewi, Log-Concave Sampling (2026-08-09), Definition 1.5.5, printed p. 39 / PDF p. 51: in the absolutely-continuous case mu << nu, D_f(mu||nu)=integral f(dmu/dnu) dnu for convex f on R_+ with f(1)=0. This child formalizes only the finite real-valued AC branch and does not claim the general singular extension.
target_statement: Introduce an explicit finite-AC domain for probability measures mu,nu and scalar f: require mu << nu, convexity on the nonnegative half-line, f(1)=0, and integrability of f applied to Samplinglib's canonical real RN density. Define the finite real value only on that domain, and prove that any nu-a.e. equal density representative yields the same integral. Do not identify this child with the full Definition 1.5.5 singular extension.

searched: Samplinglib main: no general f-divergence object; RNLogRatio.density is the canonical real RN representative
Pinned Mathlib: no Csiszar/fDivergence declaration found
Pinned Mathlib Bochner integral: usable for the finite integrable AC branch but totalized outside it
Chewi Definition 1.5.5: the AC clause is exactly the integral formalized here, while the singular correction remains in the blocked parent
shared_floor_audit.notes: The key design choice is to put integrability in the domain contract and pass a domain witness to the value definition. This prevents Mathlib's totalized real integral from being advertised as a source-faithful divergence value when the source quantity should be infinite or undefined in the finite-real sense. Convexity is required only on Ici 0 because RNLogRatio.density is nonnegative. The full singular/extended-value Definition 1.5.5 remains the separate blocked parent #230. The theorem module and focused API checks compiled without any statement repair; the same exact head passed the full ASTIS root gate and site build.
